Ivy League Tournament champions |tourney= [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result =Sweet Sixteen }} {{2022–23 Ivy League men's basketball standings}} [[File:Princeton Tiger Caden Pierce and Brown Bear Nana Owusu-Anane.jpg|thumb|right|Princeton's Caden Pierce and Brown's Nana Owusu-Anane]] The '''2022–23 Princeton Tigers men's basketball team''' represented [[Princeton University]] in the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Tigers, led by 11th-year head coach [[Mitch Henderson]], played their home games at [[Jadwin Gymnasium]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] as members of the [[Ivy League]]. The Tigers defeated No. 2 seed [[2022–23 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] to become the eleventh No. 15 seed to [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament upsets|upset]] a No. 2 seed in the Tournament's history.{{Cite web |title=March Madness 2023: Princeton shocks Arizona, No. 15 upsets a No. 2 for 11th time in NCAA Tournament history |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/march-madness-2023-princeton-shocks-arizona-no-15-upsets-a-no-2-for-11th-time-in-ncaa-tournament-history/ |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} They then defeated No. 7 seed [[2022–23 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] to become the fourth No. 15 seed to advance to the Sweet Sixteen, making it three consecutive years a No. 15 seed has accomplished the feat.{{Cite news |last=Miller |first=Scott |date=2023-03-19 |title=Princeton Follows Up Its N.C.A.A. Surprise With a Stroll to the Round of 16 |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/03/18/sports/ncaabasketball/princeton-sweet-16.html |access-date=2023-03-20 |issn=0362-4331}}{{Cite web |last=Fuente |first=Homero De la |date=2023-03-19 |title=15-seed Princeton will continue its March Madness Cinderella run, advances to Sweet 16 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/03/18/sport/princeton-missouri-ncaa-march-madness-basketball/index.html |access-date=2023-03-20 |website=CNN |language=en}} Princeton's Cinderella run came to an end with a 75–86 loss to [[2022–23 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] in the Sweet Sixteen, marking the Tigers' farthest advance in the NCAA Tournament since [[1967 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1967]]. ==Previous season== The [[2021-22 Princeton Tigers men's basketball team|Tigers]] finished the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] 23–7, 12–2 in Ivy League play to finish as Ivy League regular season champions. They defeated [[2021–22 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team|Cornell]] in the semifinals of the [[2022 Ivy League men's basketball tournament|Ivy League tournament]]{{Cite news|url=https://goprincetontigers.com/news/2022/3/12/mens-basketball-headed-to-championship-sunday-at-ivymadness.aspx|title=Men's Basketball Headed to Championship Sunday at #IvyMadness|work=Princeton University Athletics|access-date=November 29, 2022|language=en}} before losing to [[2021–22 Yale Bulldogs men's basketball team|Yale]] in the championship game.{{Cite news|url=https://ivyleague.com/news/2022/3/13/yale-tops-princeton-for-ivy-league-mens-basketball-title.aspx|title=Yale Tops Princeton For Ivy League Men's Basketball Title|work=Ivy League|access-date=November 29, 2022|language=en}} As a regular season champion who failed to win their conference tournament, the Tigers received an automatic bid to the [[2022 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]]. There they lost to [[2021–22 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]] in the first round.{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/gametracker/recap/NCAAB_20220315_PRINCE@VCU/|title=VCU
